claim: "Enquiries arrive as a call or a free-text comment with no questions on building type, size, systems or deadline, while each deliverable needs scoping plus a written proposal."
problem: The second half is stated as fact but is not in any cited source. https://stoneridgeeng.com/due-diligence.html says only that clients 'will be provided with a full report' and that the firm assesses budget requirements; it never mentions a proposal, a proposal fee, or a scoping step. The audit's own source annotation ('document deliverables needing scoping plus a written proposal') over-describes what that page supports. It is a reasonable inference from consulting practice, but it is unlabelled and the whole second opportunity (and its hour range) rests on it.
fix: Either mark it as inference - e.g. 'each deliverable is a report, so it has to be scoped and priced before work starts (our inference - nothing on the site describes a proposal step)' - or trim the claim to what the page shows: 'deliverables are written reports, not fixed-price products'.

claim: "x 25-40% automated" - the multiplier in both hour ranges (48-307 h; 24-104 h).
problem: Only the upper bound has a cited basis (40% faster on short professional writing tasks, Science 2023). The 25% low end has no source anywhere in the audit, and the ACEC URL listed in Sources (68% estimate AI could automate up to 29% of tasks) is never referenced in the body. The multiplier is also not listed among the stated assumptions in either parenthetical - those name only the proposal count, the hours each, the single principal and the weekly hours - so it reads as a measured figure rather than a transfer from a 20-30 minute writing-task experiment to scoping and fee-setting.
fix: Add the multiplier to the assumptions list and name the low end's basis: 'x 25-40% (25% from the ACEC Research Institute 2025 estimate that AI could automate up to 29% of tasks, 40% from the Science 2023 writing-task study - both transfers, not measurements at this firm)'. Keep the dollar figures; the arithmetic itself is correct.

claim: "Seen as a prospective client would, your website and Google listing are not taking new work."
problem: Overstated as a factual conclusion: the site and the Google listing both display a working phone number, (732) 658-6302, and the contact page explicitly tells visitors to call for immediate assistance. The verified failure is narrower - the web form, tap-to-call and mobile menu - which the body states accurately.
fix: Soften to what was verified, e.g. 'the only intake path that still works is the phone number; the form, the mobile menu and the listing itself are not pulling their weight.'
